title: Burn Captions into an iPhone Video for Reliable Sharing
description: Export a captioned MP4 or MOV when you want words to stay visible as part of a shared video.
direct: Export a captioned MP4 or MOV if the words need to stay visible wherever the file plays. Keep the original if you may need clean footage or a different style later.
figureAlt: Visible captions are part of the video frame while an SRT remains separate text.

cards.choice.heading: Choose permanent or editable
cards.choice.body: Burned-in captions become video pixels. They travel with that export but cannot be switched off or restyled as a separate subtitle track. Keep an uncaptioned original and an editable transcript when you need later changes.
sections.explain.heading: Preview is not the delivery file
sections.explain.body: A caption visible in an editing preview does not establish that you selected a captioned-video export. Check a few points in the saved clip with audio muted, especially after cuts. Sending the original video plus an SRT is a different workflow and may need separate import at the destination.
sections.practice.heading: Know the app options
sections.practice.body: Our iPhone app provides captioned video and SRT exports. Free single-video exports include a Just Captions watermark; Pro removes it and unlocks additional features. Core captions can run on device; optional online AI text tools require consent. This guide covers adding captions from speech, not extracting or removing words already burned into someone else’s video.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Can the viewer turn off captions I burned into the video?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: No. They are part of the picture. Deliver a clean video and a supported subtitle track when viewers need an on/off switch.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: My preview has captions but the shared video has none. What should I check?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Play the exact attachment outside the editor. If it is the uncaptioned original, select the saved captioned-video export instead.

steps.step-1.text: Import your spoken video into Subtitle Maker: Just Captions and generate captions. Correct names, words and timing before styling.
steps.step-2.text: Choose a readable caption style and preview the full frame, including faces and any existing lower-third text.
steps.step-3.text: Export a captioned MP4 or MOV. Open the saved video outside the editor and test the exact file you plan to send.
